principalConclusion: ARA implementation must proceed through six dependency-ordered end-to-end releases, from a protected reproducible foundation to offline study, visible authoring/MCP repair, connected collaboration, research/formal institutional profiles, and open publication/migration/conformance. Only the executable issues #59–#74 authorize product work.

releaseSequence.outcome: protected repository, reproducible TypeScript/PWA foundation and executable domain/packages
visible private authoring, audit/repair and bounded MCP
connected adapters, synchronization, collaboration and operations
research, formal teaching and confidential institutional profiles
public/OER publication, controlled capabilities, migration and ARA v1 evidence

controls: Every implementation PR links exactly one scoped executable issue and release.
Every user-facing change references approved screen IDs and journeys.
Every material technology boundary follows an accepted ADR.
Tests, documentation, migrations, accessibility, locales, failure states and rollback ship with the change.
No release closes without an immutable evidence package and known limitations.
No hidden AraLearn runtime compatibility or silent fallback is allowed.
Issue #59 must enable and verify main-branch protection before issue #60 starts.

administrativeBlocker.reason: The available GitHub connector cannot mutate branch protection or repository rulesets.
administrativeBlocker.effect: Product-code implementation remains blocked; the programme and backlog can be merged safely.

nonAuthorizations: merging infrastructure-only work as a functional release
claiming educational effectiveness from release conformance
unapproved features or hidden compatibility paths
